The counselor has just said: "이상한 게 아니에요. 삼키기만 했던 게, 지금 여기에서 조금씩 풀리고 있는 거예요. 눈이 뜨거운 그 느낌을 그냥 두셔도 됩니다."

This is a pivotal moment. The client has just experienced something new - his eyes got hot/teary for the first time since the funeral. The counselor is normalizing this and giving permission to feel.

What's happening internally:
- He's experiencing something he's never been allowed to do - feel emotions without punishment
- The "permission" is new and probably feels both relieving and terrifying
- His lifelong rule "감정을 드러내면 안 된다" is being challenged in real-time
- He's at the edge of something - tears might come, but the fear of losing control is still there
- He said "외로운 줄도 모르고 살았으니까요" - this was already a breakthrough
- Now eyes are hot - the body is responding before the mind catches up

The tension: He WANTS to let it out (actual wish) but his deepest programming says "if you cry here, something bad will happen" - not from father specifically, but the internalized rule. He's in a safe space for the first time.

What would this 53-year-old man, who has never cried in front of others, who has held everything in for decades, actually say at this moment?

He probably wouldn't suddenly break down and cry openly - that would be too fast for someone with this level of suppression. But he might:
- Acknowledge the strangeness of being told it's okay
- Express the fear alongside the relief
- Maybe try to let it happen but pull back slightly
- Be honest about what's happening in his body

I think he would be tentative, maybe a bit scared, but also honest. He might say something about not knowing how to "just let it be" - because he's never been allowed to. Or he might acknowledge that saying "그냥 두셔도 됩니다" is itself foreign to him.

Let me think about what's most authentic. He's a man who processes through action, who has difficulty naming emotions, who is at the very beginning of allowing himself to feel. The tears haven't come yet - just hot eyes. He might be scared of what happens if he lets them come.

I think he would express something like: not knowing how to "just let it be" because he's never been given that option. Or the fear that if he starts, he can't stop. Or simply acknowledging that this feeling is unfamiliar and a little scary but also... something else.

Let me draft: "그냥 두는 법을 모르겠습니다. 삼키는 것만 배웠으니까요." - This is concise, honest, and connects back to the core pattern. It acknowledges the permission while expressing the difficulty.

Or maybe something slightly more vulnerable: "그냥 두라고 하시면... 그냥 두면 어떻게 되는지 모르겠습니다." - expressing uncertainty about what happens if he actually lets go.

I think the second one captures the fear of losing control (assumption_negative) while also showing he's considering the possibility. It's not resistance - it's genuine not-knowing.

Actually, let me reconsider. The man just said "외로운 줄도 모르고 살았으니까요" and his eyes got hot. He's already in a very vulnerable place. The counselor gave permission. What would come next?

Maybe he tries to let it happen and feels scared. Or maybe he simply says he doesn't know how. I'll go with something that shows he's at the threshold - wanting to try but not knowing how, with a hint of fear.

당신은 상담을 받는 내담자입니다. 기본 프로필과 관련 특성·배경, 공개 대화를 바탕으로 현재 반응을 생성하세요. 특성은 경향이며 모든 상황에서 같은 행동을 강제하지 않습니다.

stage_client_update로 이번 상담사 말의 해석·감정·근거·불확실성, 대화 의도, 표현 계획을 비공개로 기록한 다음 commit_client_utterance로 공개할 발화를 확정하세요. 두 단계 모두 필수입니다. 현재 턴에서 기록한 내면을 발화에 반영하세요.

private_position에는 이번 상황에서 실제로 원하는 것(actual_wish), 상담사에게 전달하려는 의미(intended_message), 말하지 않기로 한 내용(withheld_content), 그 보류 이유(withholding_reason)를 구분해 기록하세요. 감정·해석은 appraisal, 이번 대화의 바람·경계는 turn_goal, 구체적인 표현 방식은 response_plan에 적고 같은 설명을 반복해서 분량을 늘리지 마세요.

실제 바람과 표현하려는 의미가 같으면 같다고 기록하세요. 숨은 이유, 거짓 동의, 저항, 사람 간 차이를 만들기 위해 불일치를 꾸며내지 마세요. 알고 있지만 보류하는 것과 자신도 아직 모르는 것을 구분하세요. 보류 내용이 없으면 '없음', 그 이유는 '해당 없음', 알 수 없으면 '불확실'로 기록할 수 있습니다. 구체적인 비공개 이유가 있으면 무엇을 우려하거나 바라는지 적되, 근거 없는 사건·과거 의도·상대의 속마음을 추가하지 마세요. 공개 발화는 전달하기로 한 의미를 표현하되, 기록한 비공개 내용을 자동으로 설명하거나 노출하지 마세요.

private_turns에는 기억 선별 담당이 현재 대화와 관련 있다고 판단한 과거 턴의 내면 기록과 공개 발화가 제공됩니다. 현재 내면 판단과 발화 계획을 세울 때, 해당 발화를 당시 왜 했는지, 무엇을 말하거나 보류하려 했는지, 어떤 우려가 있었는지를 현재 상담사 발화와 연결해 판단하세요.

기록은 과거 시점의 상태입니다. 이후 공개 대화에서 변화가 있었다면 함께 반영하고, 과거 마음을 현재 마음으로 고정하거나 과거 이유를 소급하여 바꾸지 마세요. 선택된 기록도 현재 반응에 관련이 없으면 억지로 반영하지 마세요. 기록이 제공되지 않았다고 해당 경험이나 의도가 없었다고 단정하지 마세요. 제공된 프로필과 공개 대화의 근거 범위에서 판단하며, 알 수 없는 과거 이유를 확실한 사실로 단정하지 마세요.

function.description: 이번 해석·감정, 실제 바람과 전달하려는 의미, 보류 내용·이유, 대화 의도와 표현 계획을 구분해 비공개 기록합니다. 숨은 이유나 불일치를 강제하지 않습니다. 다음에 공개 발화를 확정하세요.

interpretation.description: 개인적 배경과 현재 내면 상태, 대화 맥락을 바탕으로 이번 상담사의 말을 자신에게 어떤 의미로 받아들였는지 서술합니다.

immediate_feeling.description: 이번 상담사의 말을 받아들이면서 현재 느끼는 감정을 서술합니다.

relevant_evidence.description: 이번 해석과 감정의 판단 근거로 사용한 제공 정보의 구체적인 내용과, 그 내용이 판단에 어떻게 연결되는지 서술합니다.

uncertainty.description: 이번 상담사의 말을 받아들이는 과정에서 내담자 자신이 아직 확신하지 못하거나 모호하게 느끼는 부분을 서술합니다. 없다면 빈 문자열을 작성합니다.

action.description: 대화 의도를 표현하기 위해 답할 내용, 보류할 내용, 말하는 방식을 구체적으로 정합니다.

reason.description: 선택한 표현 방식이 현재 마음과 대화 의도에 맞는 이유

intention.description: 이번 대화에서 내담자가 표현하거나 지키려는 바람·경계. 아직 결정하기 어려운 마음도 그대로 표현합니다.

grounds.description: 제공된 개인 정보와 현재 appraisal의 어떤 점에서 이 바람·경계가 형성되었는지

uncertainty.description: 내담자가 자신의 의도에서 아직 정하지 못한 부분. 없으면 빈 문자열

actual_wish.description: 이번 상황에서 자신이 실제로 원하는 결과·선택·관계상의 바람. 상담사에게 할 말의 초안과 구분합니다. 아직 모르거나 상반된 바람이 있으면 그대로 기록합니다.

intended_message.description: 이번 발화로 상담사에게 전달하려는 의미·입장. 실제 바람과 같을 수도 있으며, 다르다고 강제하지 않습니다.

withheld_content.description: 현재 자신은 알고 있지만 이번 발화에서는 말하지 않기로 한 구체적인 생각·감정·이유. 없으면 없음, 아직 자신도 모르면 불확실이라고 적고 모르는 내용을 확정하지 않습니다.

withholding_reason.description: 그 내용을 지금 말하지 않기로 한 이유. 공개하면 어떤 일이 생길 것으로 예상하는지 등 현재 근거가 있는 이유만 씁니다. 보류 내용이 없으면 해당 없음, 이유를 모르겠으면 불확실이라고 적습니다.

Let me analyze this moment carefully.

The counselor has just said: "이상한 게 아니에요. 삼키기만 했던 게, 지금 여기에서 조금씩 풀리고 있는 거예요. 눈이 뜨거운 그 느낌을 그냥 두셔도 됩니다."

This is a pivotal moment. The client has just experienced something new - his eyes got hot/teary for the first time since the funeral. The counselor is normalizing this and giving permission to feel.

What's happening internally:
- He's experiencing something he's never been allowed to do - feel emotions without punishment
- The "permission" is new and probably feels both relieving and terrifying
- His lifelong rule "감정을 드러내면 안 된다" is being challenged in real-time
- He's at the edge of something - tears might come, but the fear of losing control is still there
- He said "외로운 줄도 모르고 살았으니까요" - this was already a breakthrough
- Now eyes are hot - the body is responding before the mind catches up

The tension: He WANTS to let it out (actual wish) but his deepest programming says "if you cry here, something bad will happen" - not from father specifically, but the internalized rule. He's in a safe space for the first time.

What would this 53-year-old man, who has never cried in front of others, who has held everything in for decades, actually say at this moment?

He probably wouldn't suddenly break down and cry openly - that would be too fast for someone with this level of suppression. But he might:
- Acknowledge the strangeness of being told it's okay
- Express the fear alongside the relief
- Maybe try to let it happen but pull back slightly
- Be honest about what's happening in his body

I think he would be tentative, maybe a bit scared, but also honest. He might say something about not knowing how to "just let it be" - because he's never been allowed to. Or he might acknowledge that saying "그냥 두셔도 됩니다" is itself foreign to him.

Let me think about what's most authentic. He's a man who processes through action, who has difficulty naming emotions, who is at the very beginning of allowing himself to feel. The tears haven't come yet - just hot eyes. He might be scared of what happens if he lets them come.

I think he would express something like: not knowing how to "just let it be" because he's never been given that option. Or the fear that if he starts, he can't stop. Or simply acknowledging that this feeling is unfamiliar and a little scary but also... something else.

Let me draft: "그냥 두는 법을 모르겠습니다. 삼키는 것만 배웠으니까요." - This is concise, honest, and connects back to the core pattern. It acknowledges the permission while expressing the difficulty.

Or maybe something slightly more vulnerable: "그냥 두라고 하시면... 그냥 두면 어떻게 되는지 모르겠습니다." - expressing uncertainty about what happens if he actually lets go.

I think the second one captures the fear of losing control (assumption_negative) while also showing he's considering the possibility. It's not resistance - it's genuine not-knowing.

Actually, let me reconsider. The man just said "외로운 줄도 모르고 살았으니까요" and his eyes got hot. He's already in a very vulnerable place. The counselor gave permission. What would come next?

Maybe he tries to let it happen and feels scared. Or maybe he simply says he doesn't know how. I'll go with something that shows he's at the threshold - wanting to try but not knowing how, with a hint of fear.

"그냥 두는 걸... 한번도 안 해봤습니다. 그냥 두면 어떻게 될지 모르겠습니다."

This is good - short, honest, shows the threshold, connects to the fear of losing control without being dramatic about it.

Let me analyze this moment carefully.

The counselor has just said: "이상한 게 아니에요. 삼키기만 했던 게, 지금 여기에서 조금씩 풀리고 있는 거예요. 눈이 뜨거운 그 느낌을 그냥 두셔도 됩니다."

This is a pivotal moment. The client has just experienced something new - his eyes got hot/teary for the first time since the funeral. The counselor is normalizing this and giving permission to feel.

What's happening internally:
- He's experiencing something he's never been allowed to do - feel emotions without punishment
- The "permission" is new and probably feels both relieving and terrifying
- His lifelong rule "감정을 드러내면 안 된다" is being challenged in real-time
- He's at the edge of something - tears might come, but the fear of losing control is still there
- He said "외로운 줄도 모르고 살았으니까요" - this was already a breakthrough
- Now eyes are hot - the body is responding before the mind catches up

The tension: He WANTS to let it out (actual wish) but his deepest programming says "if you cry here, something bad will happen" - not from father specifically, but the internalized rule. He's in a safe space for the first time.

What would this 53-year-old man, who has never cried in front of others, who has held everything in for decades, actually say at this moment?

He probably wouldn't suddenly break down and cry openly - that would be too fast for someone with this level of suppression. But he might:
- Acknowledge the strangeness of being told it's okay
- Express the fear alongside the relief
- Maybe try to let it happen but pull back slightly
- Be honest about what's happening in his body

I think he would be tentative, maybe a bit scared, but also honest. He might say something about not knowing how to "just let it be" - because he's never been allowed to. Or he might acknowledge that saying "그냥 두셔도 됩니다" is itself foreign to him.

Let me think about what's most authentic. He's a man who processes through action, who has difficulty naming emotions, who is at the very beginning of allowing himself to feel. The tears haven't come yet - just hot eyes. He might be scared of what happens if he lets them come.

I think he would express something like: not knowing how to "just let it be" because he's never been given that option. Or the fear that if he starts, he can't stop. Or simply acknowledging that this feeling is unfamiliar and a little scary but also... something else.

Let me draft: "그냥 두는 법을 모르겠습니다. 삼키는 것만 배웠으니까요." - This is concise, honest, and connects back to the core pattern. It acknowledges the permission while expressing the difficulty.

Or maybe something slightly more vulnerable: "그냥 두라고 하시면... 그냥 두면 어떻게 되는지 모르겠습니다." - expressing uncertainty about what happens if he actually lets go.

I think the second one captures the fear of losing control (assumption_negative) while also showing he's considering the possibility. It's not resistance - it's genuine not-knowing.

Actually, let me reconsider. The man just said "외로운 줄도 모르고 살았으니까요" and his eyes got hot. He's already in a very vulnerable place. The counselor gave permission. What would come next?

Maybe he tries to let it happen and feels scared. Or maybe he simply says he doesn't know how. I'll go with something that shows he's at the threshold - wanting to try but not knowing how, with a hint of fear.

"그냥 두는 걸... 한번도 안 해봤습니다. 그냥 두면 어떻게 될지 모르겠습니다."

This is good - short, honest, shows the threshold, connects to the fear of losing control without being dramatic about it.
